already-have.corrections: Already tracked, different mechanism: GitHub issue #601 (OPEN, priority:medium, surface:trusted-ui, source:ext-research-2026-07-31, OWNER-DECISION) 'User-personalized boot artifact rendered before PIN entry (anti lookalike-device-swap)'. #601 proposes a static user-chosen artifact stored on the MCU and is blocked because geometry/src/lib.rs:103-118 assigns every flash page an owner (only bank-2 page 127 is spare and const-asserted must-remain-erased), so it needs a geometry decision intersecting #540/#543/#545 and invariant #10. D-09 differs in two ways that matter: (1) the words are SE-keyed and PIN-prefix-dependent (Coldcard-style), so a clone running identical firmware cannot reproduce them even if it copies MCU flash, whereas a #601 artifact copied from an RDP-0-verified-then-sold unit's flash would be reproducible; (2) the per-device secret lives in an SE object (SE050 HMAC/CMAC key or OPTIGA protected object), so the #601 MCU-page geometry blocker does NOT apply — the blocker instead becomes an SE050 object/policy + attempt-counter interaction design (must not consume page-124/E120 budget; production SE050 UserID policy denies attribute reads, SW=0x6986) and the OPTIGA S-1/S-2 metadata ceremony if an OPTIGA object is chosen. Recommended delta: file as a sibling/alternative under #601 (or amend #601 to cover both mechanisms) and amend docs/security/user-device-verification.md rather than creating a new doc. Adjacent but NOT overlapping: #206 (SE050 boot-time variant assertion) and threat-model.md §7.11 rows 339-345 defend the device against a swapped *chip*, not the user against a swapped *device*; #772 (closed) 'check words' is backup verification (verify_mnemonic), unrelated. Two framing corrections to the proposal: the device is a 2-button UI, so the 'after 4 digits' hook sits inside the pin_entry.rs long-right 'next position' handler at position 3->4, and rendering must use the secret_text CT row and the F-24 forced-frame path (open #784 shows a non-forced-frame leak in the restore wizard on exactly this class of path); and on the sealed pq1 unit the FSBL fingerprint is currently invisible anyway (#705), which strengthens rather than weakens the case for a PIN-time per-device check. Not checked: Coldcard/Passport vendor source URLs (no web fetch performed); whether SE050 E2 variant on pq1 supports an HMAC/CMAC key object under the production applet config.

feasible.reason: The proposal does defend against the stated threat in its passive form: an offline look-alike/implanted unit cannot reproduce words keyed on a per-device secret the attacker never had, so the user aborts after 4 digits. It is realisable on pq1 with no hardware change (SE050 and OPTIGA are both reachable pre-PIN; the lifecycle already does SE attest before PIN entry; a CT secret-row render primitive exists at secure/src/ui/secret_text.rs:73-82; PIN_LEN is pinned to 8 at proto/src/lib.rs:21 so a 4-digit prefix leak leaves 10^4 candidates against a 10-attempt budget). kind=firmware, cost M and P2 are reasonable. However several load-bearing details in the proposal are wrong or under-stated, listed in corrections: it only raises cost against an online relay (the attacker holding the original can mirror the words in real time), the 'rate-limited by SE policy' clause is not implementable on either SE, neither driver has HMAC-generate today, the SE-keyed property only holds once the SE<->MCU tunnel keys are per-die (the still-blocked rdp2-self-lock rotation), and a DHUK-CMAC variant via the existing hw::saes_cmac::cmac_dhuk gives the same guarantee with far less surface.
feasible.corrections: 1) Only raises cost, does not prevent, against the live-relay variant of the swap: the fake relays the 4-digit prefix to the attacker who types it into the stolen original, reads the words on its screen (2 s budget is enough for real time), and the fake displays them; the user then types the remaining 4 digits and the attacker holds PIN + original. Coldcard documents this as the accepted residual; the proposal should say 'defeats offline clones, not an online relay'. The fake also always learns the 4-digit prefix before the user can abort (acceptable only because PIN_LEN=8 is fixed; a shorter PIN would make the prefix leak fatal). 2) 'Rate-limited by SE policy to ~2 s' is not realisable: SE050 object policies have no time-based throttle and OPTIGA's only rate primitives are usage counters (E120/E121 LUC), which consume budget — exactly what the proposal says must not happen. The ATECC608 in Coldcard has no timer either; the delay is firmware-enforced. Implement the 2 s hold in the secure world (S-only TIM, like timeout.rs), acceptable because under RDP-2 + TrustZone the only caller is secure firmware; do not bind the MAC object to E120/E121/UserID attempts. 3) Driver gap not flagged: secure/src/se050/ has no HMAC/MAC CryptoObject support at all (grep for hmac/INS_MAC/CryptoObject is empty), and secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs only implements HMAC *verify* (DecryptSym mode 0x20 for AuthRef, lines 160-167, 902-932), not HMAC generate or E200 CMAC. The SE route needs new APDUs plus a new OPTIGA secret object/metadata, which lands inside the still-open S-1/S-2 F1D0-class ceremony. 4) The 'clone cannot reproduce the words' claim is only true once the SE tunnels are die-bound: an attacker holding the original can transplant the SE carrying the MAC key onto a malicious board and the words follow the SE. That is blocked only after the transport->BHK (SE050) / DHUK+salt (OPTIGA PBS) rotation of the production-quarantined rdp2-self-lock candidate; under bench/OTP-hardcoded transport keys the words are reproducible. 5) Cheaper equivalent: a per-die SAES-CMAC(DHUK, prefix) via the existing hw::saes_cmac::cmac_dhuk (secure/src/hw/saes_cmac.rs:44) gives the same device-binding (a different die yields different words, DHUK never leaves SAES, no transplant dependency, no I2C traffic, no SE object design) and reuses the BIP-39 word mapping already linked for measured-boot fingerprints; its security is identical to the SE route since in both only secure firmware on the original MCU can invoke the MAC. Caveat: at RDP-0 DHUK is an ST constant (all dev boards give the same words) — fine, production self-locks to RDP-2 on first boot. With this route cost is S rather than M. 6) The words are a stable secret shown at every unlock: one filmed screen plus later possession of the device lets an attacker enumerate 10,000 prefixes (~5.5 h at 2 s) and recover 4 of 8 digits — must be stated as a residual, render via secret_glyph_cols (F-24 display-broadcast residual still applies), and the words are per-device not per-seed, so a seed restore onto a new unit yields new words (setup UX must say so). 7) Flash: any variant adds code to a ui-px image already 76,949 B over the secure slot; the DHUK route is near-zero, the SE route is not. 8) UX: the 2 s hold also applies to the correct prefix on every unlock.

vendor-claim.reason: The vendor precedent is real and novelty='parity' is correct: Coldcard ships PIN-prefix anti-phishing words computed with an SE-held secret (verified in the Mk4 bootloader source: stm32/mk4-bootloader/pins.c `pin_prefix_words` -> `pin_hash(..., PIN_PURPOSE_WORDS)` -> `ae_stretch_iter(tmp, digest, KDF_ITER_WORDS=6)`; ae.c `ae_stretch_iter` loops `ae_hmac32(KEYNUM_pin_stretch, ...)` = ATECC608 OP_SHA in HMAC mode; ae_config.h `KEYNUM_pin_stretch = 2`, Slot[2] IsSecret=1, ReqAuth=1), and Foundation Passport Core and Prime ship 'Security Words' after the first 4 PIN digits, disabled by default (docs.foundation.xyz/passport/advanced and /prime/prime-apps/settings/general/ both say 'This setting is disabled by default'). The Trezor firmware checkout contains no such feature (grep for anti-phish/security word/pin prefix over .c/.h/.py/.rs/.md returns only font/wordlist prefix hits), and Ledger has no pre-PIN device-authenticity words (only the online genuine-check challenge-response attestation and an unkeyed custom lock-screen image on Stax/Flex). The cited sources support the claim. Only mechanism details of the Coldcard precedent are stated imprecisely (see corrections), which does not change the precedent or novelty verdict.
vendor-claim.corrections: 1) Coldcard mechanism, per code not blog: the delay is NOT an SE policy/rate-limit of 2 s; it is 6 iterations (`#define KDF_ITER_WORDS 6 // about 1.4s (measured)`) of ATECC608 HMAC-SHA256 (`ae_hmac32(KEYNUM_pin_stretch, end, end)`, OP_SHA with HMAC_Init/Finalize flags), each requiring `ae_pair_unlock()`; the comment says 'rate limiting factor here is communication time w/ 608a, not algos'. The blog's '2 seconds per prefix' is a rounded figure. The keyed object is the SAME `KEYNUM_pin_stretch` slot used for PIN stretching, not a dedicated words key, so the proposal's 'separate keyed object, never the PIN object' is stricter than Coldcard, not parity. 2) The pre-hash is not just 'hashed PIN prefix': `pin_hash()` = SHA-256(hash_cache_secret || purpose || prefix || pairing_secret) -> `se2_pin_hash()` (SE2, DS28C36, also involved) -> SHA-256; 32 bits are taken, 22 bits (2 BIP-39 words) shown. 3) Coldcard's own comments state 'result here is not confidential' / 'hash generated is shown on bus' — the SE1 bus is plaintext single-wire; PQSigner's Shielded Connection/SCP03 tunnels (invariant #3) would be an improvement over the precedent, worth stating. 4) Prefix length: Coldcard's prefix is user-chosen 2-6 digits (coldcard.com/docs/pins), not fixed 4; the fixed 'after the first 4 digits' pause is Passport's design (Core and Prime). 5) coldcard.com/docs/pins/ supports existence and the prefix/suffix split but says nothing about the SE or a rate limit — only the coinkite Mk4 blog does; the Passport source could not be fetched (raw GitHub 404, code search empty), so Passport's SE mechanism is unverified from code. 6) Trezor analogs worth naming as non-precedent: the user-set lockscreen label shown before PIN (core/src/apps/homescreen/__init__.py:89-92 `run_lockscreen(label=storage.device.get_label(), ...)`, core/src/trezor/ui/layouts/homescreen.py:118-135) is unkeyed and trivially cloned; `core/src/apps/management/authenticate_device.py:9-60` is host-driven Optiga/Tropic challenge attestation (`optiga.sign(optiga.DEVICE_ECC_KEY_INDEX, ...)`), not an at-PIN-entry user-visible check. Trezor's counter-bound OPTIGA PIN-HMAC key (core/embed/sec/optiga/optiga.c:43-50: OID 0xF1D8 limited by counter OID 0xE122) is a directly reusable design template on the same OPTIGA Trust M family for a usage-count-bounded (rather than time-bounded) words key. 7) Ledger: Coldcard's and AirGap's comparison tables mark Ledger, Trezor, BitBox02, Jade, Keystone as lacking anti-phishing words (vendor claims, not audits); no Ledger doc describes one.
